title: AWS Cognito
summary: User pool discovery and hosted UI endpoints. Includes an enterprise test plan (jobs starting ent-).
description: Load tests an Amazon Cognito user pool: the discovery document, the JSON web key set, and the hosted UI login page, token (client credentials) and userinfo endpoints. Cognito enforces request quotas, so use a test pool and watch for throttling responses.

variables.name: url
variables.description: Issuer / base URL, no trailing slash
variables.guide: The address of the system to test, starting with https:// (or http://) and with no trailing slash, for example https://staging.example.com. Use a system you own, ideally a staging copy. BLASTA runs in a container, so for a service on your own machine use host.docker.internal instead of localhost.

variables.name: clientId
variables.description: A test client registered for load testing
variables.guide: The ID of a client registered for this test. Create a dedicated test client in your identity provider (Clients / Applications) and copy its client ID. Do not reuse a production client.

variables.name: clientSecret
variables.description: Client secret. Read from the OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET env var by the CLI.

variables.name: redirectUri
variables.description: A redirect URI registered on that client
variables.guide: A redirect URI that is registered on that client. Copy one from the client's settings: an unregistered one is refused.

variables.name: scope
variables.guide: The scopes to request, URL-encoded with %20 between them, for example openid%20profile%20email.

variables.name: token
variables.description: A valid access token. Read from OIDC_ACCESS_TOKEN by the CLI.

variables.name: poolId
variables.description: User pool id, such as us-east-1_AbCdEf
variables.guide: The user pool ID. In AWS: Cognito → User pools → your pool → User pool ID, for example us-east-1_AbCdEf.

variables.name: hostedUi
variables.description: Hosted UI domain, no trailing slash
variables.guide: The hosted UI domain. Cognito → your pool → App integration → Domain.

jobs.name: OIDC discovery document
jobs.notes: This is a hosted identity service: check the vendor's load-testing policy and your tenant's rate limits before running, keep the rate low, and expect 429s. Fetched by every relying party at start-up and on a timer. Cheap, but often served uncached.

jobs.name: discovery document (cache bypass)
jobs.notes: This is a hosted identity service: check the vendor's load-testing policy and your tenant's rate limits before running, keep the rate low, and expect 429s. Forces the origin to build the document. Shows the cost behind a CDN or cache.

jobs.name: JSON web key set
jobs.notes: This is a hosted identity service: check the vendor's load-testing policy and your tenant's rate limits before running, keep the rate low, and expect 429s. Every API validating tokens locally refreshes keys from here, and a key rotation causes a thundering herd of fetches.

jobs.name: hosted UI token: client credentials
jobs.notes: Counts against Cognito's token request quota.

jobs.name: AWS Cognito: 01 smoke
jobs.notes: Enterprise plan, step 1 of 10. One request a second for 30 seconds. Run this first, every time: it proves the address, credentials and headers are right and that the environment is up before any real load is applied. Gate: zero errors. Reference request: OIDC discovery document. Hosted identity service: this stays well below the vendor's rate limits; check their load-testing policy first.

jobs.name: AWS Cognito: 02 baseline (20% load)
jobs.notes: Step 2 of 10. About a fifth of normal traffic for 5 minutes: the uncontended latency of this request. Every later result is judged against it, so record p50 and p95. Gate: at most 0.5% errors and the default latency targets. Reference request: OIDC discovery document. Hosted identity service: this stays well below the vendor's rate limits; check their load-testing policy first.

jobs.name: AWS Cognito: 03 average load (SLO check)
jobs.notes: Step 3 of 10. Normal busy-hour traffic for 10 minutes. The rate is the reference job's rate: raise it to your measured production peak-hour rate. This is the run that proves (or breaks) your SLO. Gate: at most 1% errors, p95 and p99 inside the targets. Reference request: OIDC discovery document. Hosted identity service: this stays well below the vendor's rate limits; check their load-testing policy first.

jobs.name: AWS Cognito: 04 peak load (2x average)
jobs.notes: Step 4 of 10. Twice the average for 10 minutes: the busiest hour of the year plus headroom. Latency may rise, but must stay in SLO; if it does not, you have no headroom. Gate: at most 2% errors, latency targets doubled. Reference request: OIDC discovery document. Hosted identity service: this stays well below the vendor's rate limits; check their load-testing policy first.

jobs.name: AWS Cognito: 08 soak (30 min at 60%)
jobs.notes: Step 8 of 10, shortened for a hosted service. Steady load for 30 minutes to catch token or session expiry problems and slow decay on your side. Reference request: OIDC discovery document. Hosted identity service: this stays well below the vendor's rate limits; check their load-testing policy first.

OIDC_ACCESS_TOKEN.label: Access token
OIDC_ACCESS_TOKEN.guide:
Request one with the client-credentials grant:
`curl -s -d grant_type=client_credentials -d client_id=CLIENT -d client_secret=SECRET -d scope=openid https://IDP/token`
then copy `access_token` from the answer. Add scope=openid so userinfo calls are allowed.
It expires quickly (often 5 minutes): request a fresh one right before the run, or lengthen the token lifespan on the test client.

OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET.label: Client secret
OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET.guide: In your identity provider open the test client and go to its Credentials (or Secrets) tab, then copy the client secret. Use a dedicated test client, never a production one.
